title: Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit spectral universality
statement: Identify a precise class of deterministic quantum Hamiltonians with chaotic classical limits and prove convergence of their unfolded local spectral correlations to the appropriate random-matrix law as hbar tends to zero. The hypotheses must account for discrete and antiunitary symmetries and exclude or explain arithmetic exceptions.
assumptions: Specify the Hamiltonian family, energy window, unfolding and test-function class.
Resolve symmetry sectors before comparing spectra; time-reversal symmetry alone is not a complete classification for all spin systems.
Classical ergodicity by itself is not asserted to imply random-matrix statistics.
physics_motivation: Explains why very different chaotic quantum systems exhibit the same energy-level fluctuations.
resolution_target: A universality theorem for an explicitly defined deterministic class, including its symmetry class and exceptional cases. A numerical spacing histogram is evidence, not a theorem.
status_note: The source catalog lists the general characterization as open. Semiclassical orbit expansions and random-matrix calculations give important partial explanations. A recent-literature and exception-by-exception audit is still required.

title: GOE pair correlation for a concrete chaotic billiard
statement: Choose an explicit two-dimensional dispersing billiard with compact configuration space and specified Dirichlet obstacle boundaries, and prove that its high-energy Laplacian spectrum, unfolded within a fixed symmetry sector, has the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble two-point correlation in a stated distributional limit.
assumptions: Give the geometry and all boundary conditions, for example a finite-horizon Sinai billiard on a torus with fixed convex obstacles.
Remove geometrical symmetry degeneracies; use a spinless time-reversal-invariant system.
Define spectral smoothing and test functions independently of the eigenvalues being tested.
physics_motivation: Seeks a rigorous instance of universal level repulsion in a deterministic quantum particle system.
resolution_target: A pair-correlation convergence theorem for the specified billiard. A small-time form-factor asymptotic would be a narrower milestone, not the full result.
status_note: PubPhys records this as a special case of BGS. The exact geometry and averaging prescription must be frozen before use as a formal benchmark; this record does not claim that all ergodic billiards obey the same statistics.

title: Berry–Tabor spacing statistics beyond pair correlation
aliases: Poisson spacings in integrable quantum systems
statement: For the Dirichlet Laplacian on a rectangle, whose rescaled eigenvalues are m² + alpha n² with positive integers m,n, prove an exponential nearest-neighbor spacing law after Weyl unfolding for almost every positive aspect parameter alpha. Specify the precise energy averaging and the treatment of degeneracies.
assumptions: Use m,n greater than or equal to one, avoiding the sign degeneracies of the unreduced torus spectrum.
The target is an almost-everywhere statement in the aspect parameter, not every irrational rectangle.
Higher correlations and nearest-neighbor spacings are stronger targets than pair correlation alone.
physics_motivation: Tests the predicted distinction between uncorrelated integrable spectra and level-repelling chaotic spectra.
resolution_target: Convergence of the unfolded nearest-neighbor spacing distribution to exp(-s), with a rigorous exceptional-set statement.
status_note: The discovery source marks the family partially resolved because pair-correlation results exist. Only the stronger spacing target is retained here; precise assumptions and later advances require specialist checking.

title: Hilbert–Pólya: a quantum operator for the Riemann zeros
statement: Construct a Hilbert space and a self-adjoint operator H, defined without using the zeta zeros as input, and prove that all nontrivial zeros rho of the Riemann zeta function are exactly rho = 1/2 + iE with E in the spectrum of H, with the appropriate multiplicities and both signs. Establish the spectral identity for all nontrivial zeros, rather than only those already known to lie on the critical line.
assumptions: Specify the operator domain, self-adjointness and spectral type.
An operator defined by placing already-known zeros on its diagonal does not meet the independence requirement.
Matching the smooth counting function or finitely many zeros is not an exact spectral identification.
physics_motivation: Connects the Riemann zeros to the spectrum of a hypothetical quantum system and to signatures of quantum chaos. Included explicitly as a physics–number-theory bridge.
resolution_target: An independently defined self-adjoint operator and a rigorous identity accounting for every nontrivial zero. Self-adjointness would then force their real parts to equal one half.
status_note: The source lists the spectral construction as open. Candidate trace formulas and numerical spectral matches must not be confused with a proof. This entry is the requested exception to the catalog's usual exclusion of pure-number-theory questions.

title: GUE pair correlation of the Riemann zeros beyond restricted Fourier support
statement: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, prove Montgomery's full pair-correlation conjecture for high zeta zeros: after local mean-spacing normalization, distinct-zero pair statistics converge to the GUE density 1 - (sin(pi u)/(pi u))² for an appropriate unrestricted class of test functions, rather than only the established restricted-Fourier-support class.
assumptions: Make the height averaging, zero multiplicities and normalization explicit.
Separate the diagonal delta contribution from the correlation of distinct zeros.
The Fourier-side plateau is an asymptotic high-height limit, not an identity for a finite zero sample.
The Riemann hypothesis is an assumption of this formulation, not its conclusion.
physics_motivation: Tests the random-matrix correspondence linking prime-number fluctuations and chaotic quantum spectra.
resolution_target: A proof of full pair-correlation convergence with the support restriction removed. Extending the admissible support is partial progress; finite numerical agreement is evidence.
status_note: The discovery source lists the full-support conjecture as open. Pair correlation alone is weaker than all GUE higher correlations or the full nearest-neighbor spacing law. Retained as the requested Riemann-zero exception.

title: Quantum unique ergodicity on negatively curved surfaces
statement: For a compact smooth Riemannian surface without boundary and with strictly negative curvature, prove or disprove that every high-energy normalized Laplace eigenfunction sequence has Liouville measure as its unique semiclassical measure on the unit cotangent bundle.
assumptions: No Hecke-eigenfunction hypothesis or arithmetic symmetry is imposed.
Consider the full sequence, not merely a density-one subsequence.
Equidistribution in configuration space follows from the stated phase-space target but is a weaker assertion.
physics_motivation: Asks whether classical chaotic motion forbids persistent concentration of any high-energy quantum eigenstate.
resolution_target: A full-sequence phase-space equidistribution theorem for the stated class, or a negatively curved counterexample with a non-Liouville semiclassical measure.
status_note: Quantum ergodicity supplies density-one results, and arithmetic settings have stronger theorems. Known counterexamples in other geometries do not settle this negative-curvature formulation. The source's configuration-space question is refined here to the standard phase-space target.

title: Gaussian amplitude statistics for deterministic chaotic eigenfunctions
statement: For a specified compact negatively curved surface and a real normalized Laplace eigenbasis, establish conditions under which the values sqrt(vol(M)) phi_j(x), sampled with x uniform on M, converge in distribution to a standard real Gaussian along a density-one high-energy subsequence.
assumptions: Specify the surface, eigenbasis and handling of eigenvalue multiplicities.
Use real eigenfunctions; complex symmetry classes have different amplitude statistics.
Distributional convergence, convergence of all moments and bounds on extreme peaks are separate assertions.
physics_motivation: Would justify the random-wave description of spatial fluctuations in quantum-chaotic stationary states.
resolution_target: A deterministic eigenfunction Gaussian-limit theorem with explicit hypotheses. Establishing selected Gaussian moments would be partial progress, not the complete local random-wave process.
status_note: The source lists the amplitude-distribution problem as open. This formulation deliberately avoids treating a single moment or a sup-norm bound as equivalent to the entire random-wave conjecture.

title: Quantitative ETH for a nonintegrable local Hamiltonian
statement: For an explicitly specified nonintegrable finite-range spin Hamiltonian, derive quantitative diagonal and off-diagonal eigenstate-thermalization estimates for fixed-support observables in a bulk microcanonical energy window as the system size grows. Identify whether the conclusion concerns almost all eigenstates or every eigenstate in the window.
assumptions: Fix the model, couplings, boundary conditions, energy density and symmetry sector.
Account for conserved quantities and do not assume that nonintegrability by itself excludes many-body scars.
Specify the scale of matrix-element fluctuations and the measure over eigenstates or samples.
physics_motivation: Seeks a microscopic explanation of why isolated quantum matter becomes locally thermal under unitary dynamics.
resolution_target: A theorem with vanishing finite-size errors for a physically local nonintegrable model, or an explicit obstruction to a precisely stated ETH claim.
status_note: An editorial research target guided by the ETH review, not a claim that every version of ETH is unproved. Random-matrix, typical-state, weak-ETH and special-model results must be separated from the chosen deterministic Hamiltonian target.

title: The random-matrix energy scale of ETH matrix elements
statement: For a specified chaotic local many-body Hamiltonian and local observable, determine how the energy scale below which its eigenbasis matrix elements exhibit random-matrix correlations depends on system size, conservation laws and transport. Distinguish this scale from the onset of spectral correlations and from the bandwidth of the ETH envelope.
assumptions: Fix the energy-density window and all exact symmetry sectors.
Define the matrix-element correlation statistic and a quantitative criterion for approaching its random-matrix limit.
State separately what follows from diffusion assumptions and what is derived from microscopic dynamics.
physics_motivation: Connects slow hydrodynamic modes to the microscopic limits of random-matrix descriptions of quantum matter.
resolution_target: A controlled scaling law with analytic error estimates or a reproducible numerical determination with stated finite-size uncertainty for the selected observable and model.
status_note: The source lists the scale question as open. Numerical determination in a fixed family is a useful scoped deliverable; an extrapolated scaling law is not a general theorem about ETH.

title: Thermalization times under weak integrability breaking
statement: For a fixed interacting integrable chain H0 perturbed by a specified local term gV, derive the decay rates of its formerly conserved charges and the crossover from a generalized Gibbs ensemble to thermal equilibrium as g tends to zero. Determine when a rate proportional to g² is justified and when selection rules or hydrodynamic effects change the scaling.
assumptions: Fix H0, V, the initial ensemble and observables; identify charges that remain exactly conserved.
State the order of thermodynamic, weak-coupling and long-time limits.
Do not infer a thermodynamic relaxation rate solely from finite-size avoided crossings.
physics_motivation: Explains how a nearly integrable isolated quantum system eventually forgets its extra conserved quantities.
resolution_target: A controlled kinetic limit or quantitatively converged numerical crossover for a frozen model, with explicit uncertainty and separation of prethermal and final thermal regimes.
status_note: The source separates a broad crossover question from a golden-rule scaling subproblem. They are consolidated here as one family rather than counted twice; restricted kinetic derivations are partial answers.

title: Derive the spectral ramp and Thouless time from a local Hamiltonian
statement: For a specified deterministic nonintegrable spin chain, derive the connected, appropriately energy-smoothed spectral form factor from its microscopic dynamics and identify the onset and range of the universal random-matrix ramp before the Heisenberg time.
assumptions: Fix the Hamiltonian and resolve every exact symmetry sector.
Define smoothing, unfolding, normalization and the order of size and time limits.
Retain the effects of conservation laws; a random-matrix ensemble is not substituted for the Hamiltonian as an assumption.
physics_motivation: Relates universal level correlations to the actual time scales on which an interacting quantum system becomes chaotic.
resolution_target: A controlled microscopic derivation of the ramp and its onset scale. A well-converged numerical scaling study can resolve a specified finite-model target, but does not prove universality for all local systems.
status_note: Random-matrix form factors themselves are known. This editorial target concerns their derivation in a frozen deterministic local model; solvable circuits, ensemble averages and semiclassical arguments cover different scopes.

title: Thermodynamic fate of the PXP many-body scar tower
statement: For the periodic even-length PXP chain H = sum_i P_(i-1) X_i P_(i+1) in the blockade-constrained Hilbert space, determine the large-system fate of the anomalous finite-energy-density eigenstate tower associated with the alternating product state. Quantify its spacing, entanglement, overlap weights and local nonthermal observables as chain length increases.
assumptions: Use the undeformed PXP Hamiltonian and distinguish it from engineered exact-scar variants.
Separate exact isolated eigenstates from the proposed extensive approximate tower.
A global return probability and a local-observable revival can have different thermodynamic limits.
physics_motivation: Asks whether clean interacting quantum matter can retain a structured nonthermal sector at arbitrarily large size.
resolution_target: Controlled asymptotics proving survival or dissolution of a precisely defined scar tower, with converged numerical bounds as intermediate evidence.
status_note: Existence of finite-size scars is established evidence, not the open target. PubPhys lists the undeformed-model thermodynamic fate as open; later model-specific results and symmetry sectors need detailed checking.

title: Scrambling fronts in interacting Hamiltonian systems
statement: For a specified interacting local spin Hamiltonian at fixed temperature, determine the asymptotic spreading and broadening of a local operator using a precisely normalized squared commutator or out-of-time-order correlator. Derive the front velocity and broadening law from the microscopic dynamics, including the effects of conserved densities.
assumptions: Freeze the Hamiltonian, operators, thermal state and spatial dimension.
Distinguish a Lieb–Robinson upper bound from the actual butterfly velocity.
Specify the window of space-time scaling; random circuits and large-N models are comparison models, not the chosen Hamiltonian.
physics_motivation: Quantifies how initially local quantum information spreads through interacting matter.
resolution_target: A controlled analytical front law or a reproducible, convergence-tested numerical determination for the fixed model. A universal assertion across Hamiltonians requires additional hypotheses and proof.
status_note: This is a scoped research program, not the already established chaos bound under its assumptions. Known solvable models and rigorous propagation bounds do not uniquely fix the actual front in a general interacting Hamiltonian.

title: Black-hole spectral statistics in a single holographic theory
statement: For a fixed holographic boundary theory in finite spatial volume and a specified black-hole energy window, derive the random-matrix-like late-time connected spectral statistics from controlled boundary or bulk calculations. Explain how the calculation describes a single theory after a defined energy or time smoothing, rather than only an average over different Hamiltonians.
assumptions: Fix the theory, symmetry sector, large-N limit and smoothing prescription.
Distinguish ensemble-averaged toy gravity models from a fixed ultraviolet-complete boundary theory.
State how nonperturbative effects and the discreteness of the spectrum enter the late-time limit.
physics_motivation: Tests how chaotic microscopic energy levels emerge from a gravitational description of black holes.
resolution_target: A controlled single-theory derivation with a matching boundary observable, including the domain of validity of ramp and plateau predictions.
status_note: The cited work develops late-time random-matrix evidence and estimates. This entry selects the stronger fixed-theory derivation target; it does not list known ensemble calculations as unsolved or claim a complete recent holography audit.
